summary: George County tower the Mississippi Forest Service completed in 1929: 100 ft (30.5 m) galvanized steel; the Forest Lookouts site lists it as removed, with no date.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed on the Forest Lookouts site; no removal date is given.

events.note: Completed in the week ending September 30, 1929, two and a half miles west of Bendale

evidence.supports: built 1929 by the Mississippi Forest Service; 100-ft tower completed in week ending Sept. 30, 2.5 miles west of Bendale
evidence.quote: During the week ending Sept., 30, the Mississippi Forest Service completed a new 100-ft., lookout tower two and one-half miles west of Bendale.

evidence.supports: spelling Bendale; September 1929 report; material shipped; placed within two weeks; Kimball
evidence.quote: A new tower is to be erected at Bendale, George county, the material for it having been shipped last week and the tower will be placed within two weeks, Mr. Kimball said.

evidence.supports: galvanized steel, Bessemer Galvanizing Works, ladder type
evidence.quote: This tower is of galvanized steel and was manufactured by the Bessemer Galvanizing Works, Inc., and is known as the ladder type.

evidence.supports: five-man crew took about four and a half days
evidence.quote: occupied the time of a five-man crew four four and one-half days

evidence.supports: fifth tower built in two years; six towers for the coming fire season
evidence.quote: This is the fifth tower built by the Mississippi Forest Service during the last two years and makes six towers which will be in operation during the coming fire season.

evidence.supports: view over Pascagoula River and Red and Black creeks; smoke from plants at Lucedale, Moss Point, Wiggins, Maxie, Hattiesburg visible
evidence.quote: The valleys of Pascagoula River, Red and Black creeks lie within the protective radius of this tower and smoke from the manufacturing plants of Lucedale, Moss Point, Wiggins, Maxie and Hattiesburg are plainly visible on clear days.

evidence.supports: telephone connection to other Pascagoula-area towers and to wardens, rangers and smoke-chasers
evidence.quote: This tower will be connected by telephone lines with the other towers in the Pascagoula Area and with the wardens, rangers and smoke-chasers of this protective organization.

evidence.supports: survey mark listed as Benndale State Forest lot has no written description
Mississippi Forestry Commission founded March 6, 1926, in response to widespread forest fires
evidence.quote: Founded on March 6, 1926, the Mississippi Forestry Commission was created in response to widespread forest fires and the need for organized forest protection across the state.

sources.title: Governor Tate Reeves Signs Proclamation Recognizing 100 Years of the MFC

notes_for_editor: Two 1929 newspaper reports (Sun Herald, Stone County Enterprise) are known only as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspapers were not reached. The record point may be the community rather than the tower: the October 1929 report puts the tower 2.5 miles west of Bendale. The 100-ft figure is the newspaper's, not a cab-floor height. The sources do not say whether the 1929 Mississippi Forest Service is the same body as today's Mississippi Forestry Commission, so the story keeps them separate. No removal date or site description found; two searches gave nothing specific.
